theorem Over.relSectionsMap_dualNumberSections {W : C.left.Opens}
    (hW : IsCompact (W : Set C.left)) (hW' : IsQuasiSeparated (W : Set C.left))
    (x : DualNumber Γ(C.left, W)) :
    relSectionsMap C (DualNumber k) k W (Over.dualNumberSections C hW hW' x)
      = Over.sectionsBaseChange C k hW hW' (TrivSqZeroExt.fst x ⊗ₜ (1 : k)) := by
  have hA := Over.relSectionsMap_sectionsBaseChange_tmul C hW hW' (TrivSqZeroExt.fst x)
    (1 : DualNumber k)
  have hB := Over.relSectionsMap_sectionsBaseChange_tmul C hW hW' (TrivSqZeroExt.snd x)
    (ε : DualNumber k)
  rw [algebraMap_eps_eps, TensorProduct.tmul_zero, map_zero] at hB
  rw [map_one] at hA
  rw [Over.dualNumberSections_apply, baseChangeAlgEquiv_symm_apply, map_add]
  refine ((relSectionsMap C (DualNumber k) k W).map_add _ _).trans ?_
  rw [hA, hB]
  exact add_zero _

/-- **(b-coeff) on units**: the reduction of the unit attached to `u : (Γ(C, W)[ε])ˣ` is the
unit attached to `unitsFst u = fst u`.

intertwining has to be stated on `Units`. Obtained from

    (hW : IsCompact (W : Set C.left)) (hW' : IsQuasiSeparated (W : Set C.left))
    (u : (DualNumber Γ(C.left, W))ˣ) :

        (Over.dualNumberSectionsUnits C hW hW' u) :
          Γ(relCurve C k, (fst C (overSpec k k)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W))
      = Over.sectionsBaseChange C k hW hW'
          ((unitsFst u : Γ(C.left, W)) ⊗ₜ (1 : k)) :=

name: defeq-verdict-does-not-survive-a-functor
description: Proving f = g by rfl licenses nothing about F f = F g — Spec.map is functorial only propositionally, and I shipped a false claim by carrying a ring-level defeq across it.
metadata:

---

In AJCR Wave-5 T4 (run 0073 r4) I established `CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k) = 𝟙 _` by `rfl`,
and concluded — in a worksheet section I then **committed** — that `overSpec k k` and the monoidal
unit `Over.mk (𝟙 _)` were therefore the same object "by the same `rfl`", so a residual sub-item was
free. False. `Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k)) = 𝟙 (Spec k)` is **not** `rfl`; it is `Spec.map_id`,
a theorem. The two objects are equal but not *definitionally* equal, so the whiskered morphisms
`relCurveMap C k[ε] k` and `(C ◁ overDualNumberZero k).left` have **different types** — `lake build`
refuted the `congr`-plus-`rfl` attempt with a type mismatch, not a proof failure.

**Why:** a defeq verdict is about two *terms*. It transfers to `F f` and `F g` only when `F`'s action
is itself definitional, and for `Spec.map`, and most category-level constructions in mathlib, it is
not — `Spec.map_id` and `Spec.map_comp` exist precisely *because* they are theorems.

**How to apply:** re-run `rfl` at every level you intend to use it at; one `#check` per level. Be
especially suspicious when a neighbouring item genuinely *is* `rfl` — here the sibling sub-item was
`rfl` one `Spec.map` away, and that success is what made the false claim plausible. When pricing an
"identify these two objects" step, unfold to the underlying morphism, then test `rfl` at the object
level too, not only at the ring level.

Second-order, and the more useful half: the same session had just written that its predictions "held
for the first time in this lane", and the very next prediction in that family was wrong. A run of
correct predictions is not evidence the next one needs less checking — writing down that a streak has
started is a good way to stop checking.
